item.title: Kobe Luminarie: Lights of Remembrance — Guide
item.description: Kobe Luminarie is not simply a Christmas illumination. It was created in the winter of 1995, months after the Great Hanshin earthquake killed more than six thousand people and levelled much of the city, as a memorial to the dead and a signal that Kobe would recover. Designed by Italian artists and using techniques from the illuminated festivals of southern Italy, it raises vast arcades and a cathedral-like frontage of hand-painted lightwork over the streets near the old foreign settlement.

item.title: Himeyuri Peace Museum Guide: Access & What to Know
item.description: The Himeyuri Peace Memorial Museum in Itoman, in southern Okinawa, tells one of the most moving stories of the Battle of Okinawa (1945). The “Himeyuri” were a group of around 200 teenage schoolgirls and their teachers mobilised as a student nursing corps; most lost their lives in the final weeks of the battle. The museum and adjacent monument, built where many died, preserve their testimonies, photographs and belongings as a powerful plea for peace.
